title: v1.16.0
featureLines: **5.1 output.** When the source has 6 or more channels and the default output device does too, the player now outputs 5.1. Otherwise it outputs stereo. A 7.1 source folds to 5.1 (#175).

title: v0.37.0
featureLines: **Hands look like hands.** Each tracked hand is now drawn as one continuous, translucent skinned surface instead of a set of capsules. Set `DXR_MODELVIEWER_HANDS_LOOK=capsules` to get the old look back.
**Pinch works the same at any hand scale.** The pinch thresholds follow the tracked palm length, so a hand mapped with a gain, or scaled to the window, pinches at the same finger posture.

**Pinch-drag turns the model by the same amount in any window size.** Drag distance is measured in full-display metres, so a drag across a small window turns the model as far as the same drag across the whole screen.

**macOS transparent background.** Ctrl/Cmd+T switches to a see-through background with click-through (clicks outside the model reach the desktop) and keeps the window above others, as on Windows and Linux.

Hands: the rigged GenericHand mesh from the Ultraleap Unity plug-in (Apache-2.0), embedded as an asset and CPU-skinned from the 26 OpenXR hand-tracking joints; capsules stay available via `DXR_MODELVIEWER_HANDS_LOOK=capsules` (#183).

macOS: transparent background (Ctrl/Cmd+T, `MODEL_TRANSPARENT=1` / `--transparent`), alpha-coverage click-through, keep-above while transparent, and `XR_DXR_depth_budget` clip-plane support (#181, #182).

title: DisplayXR v2.33.0
featureLines: **Android arm64 (Vulkan) (#418).** The display provider now runs in an Android player against the DisplayXR runtime APK (v2.47.0+, tested v2.53.0). Tested on a Nubia Pad 2: correct stereo, 60 fps unpinned (the same as the runtime's bare …
It reuses the Linux Vulkan own-device + bridge model, with an Android-only GPU-ordered bridge copy (Unity's queue → `SYNC_FD` semaphore → one batched copy).
It loads the runtime through the Khronos Android loader (1.1.63).
The provider draws into its own `SurfaceView`, bound with `XR_DXR_android_surface_binding`.
Touch goes to Unity, and a copy goes to the runtime (`xrSubmitAndroidInputEventDXR`). The samples' input controller gets touch gestures.

The package ships the runtime-discovery manifest entries (`DisplayXR.androidlib`), the loader, and the runtime's `VK_LAYER_DXR_queue_lock` layer. It adds R8 keep rules for minified builds and turns off Unity's stock splash on Android.
Built by CI (`build-android` job, `native~/build-android.sh`); the `.so` files ship on the `upm` branch.
Setup: README § *Android (arm64, Vulkan)*; internals: `docs~/architecture/xr-display-provider.md` § *Android*.
